result.stdout:
retrograde 0.1.0-alpha: plays Commodore 64 games, and only that.

usage: retrograde <game> [options]

  <game>             a .t64, .prg, .d64 or .g64 file, or a folder holding them; the disk
                     images beside a disk are the game's other disks, in name order.
                     The folder's VERSION.NFO and retrograde.json set how it is played;
                     the options below override them

options:
  --roms <folder>    where the KERNAL, BASIC, character and 1541 ROMs are (or
                     RETROGRADE_ROMS; otherwise a roms folder next to retrograde)
  --scale <n>        the window's first size, n times the picture (3)
  --fullscreen       start in full screen
  --square-pixels    square pixels, not a PAL television's slightly narrow ones
  --port <1|2>       the joystick port the arrows and gamepads drive (the game's, or 2)
  --cursor-keys      the arrow keys are the C64's cursor keys, not the joystick
  --no-auto-warp     load at the 1541's own speed, not at full speed while its motor runs
  --no-sound         no sound
  --frames <n>       stop after n frames (50 a second)
  --screenshot <f>   save the picture as a PNG when stopping
  --headless         no window: run --frames frames and stop

playing:
  arrows, Alt/Option the joystick (unless --cursor-keys); a gamepad's d-pad or left stick
  and any face button too, and its Start button is SPACE
  keys are where they are on a C64: - is +, = is -, [ is @, ] is *, \ is ↑, ; is :,
  ' is ;, Page Down is =, ` is ←, End is £, Home is CLR/HOME, Tab is CTRL, left Ctrl is
  C=, Esc is RUN/STOP, Page Up is RESTORE
  F9 and F10 the game's previous and next disk; F11 or Alt+Enter full screen; F12 warp
  on and off; Ctrl+Alt+A pixel shape; Ctrl+Alt+S saves the game as it is, Ctrl+Alt+L
  loads it back (one save a game, kept with your settings)
